about.title: Coalinga Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Coalinga is a small city, and many residents rely on a limited number of local clinics and hospitals, or travel elsewhere in Fresno County for specialized care. When something goes wrong during that care, whether it's a missed diagnosis, a surgical error, or a medication mistake, families are often left with more questions than answers. California's medical malpractice laws, known as MICRA, impose specific requirements that don't apply to typical injury cases, including a 90-day pre-suit notice and a requirement for qualified medical expert review. These claims move on a tighter timeline than most people expect, and gathering medical records from a rural or regional facility can take time. Our team handles medical malpractice claims for Fresno County residents. We can review what happened and explain whether the facts support a claim, with no fee owed unless there's a recovery.

items.title: Deadlines Are Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: California generally allows one year from when you discover the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, to bring a claim. We can help identify which deadline applies before it passes.

items.title: A 90-Day Notice Comes First
items.desc: Before a malpractice lawsuit can be filed in California, the law requires a 90-day notice to the healthcare provider. Missing this step can delay or jeopardize a valid claim, so early legal guidance matters.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: A bad outcome by itself doesn't prove malpractice; California generally requires a qualified medical expert to support the claim. We can help arrange that review as part of evaluating your case.

items.question: I had a bad outcome from surgery in Coalinga. Does that mean malpractice happened?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law requires proof that a provider failed to meet the accepted standard of care, and a poor result on its own isn't enough. We can review your records with the help of a medical expert to see whether the treatment fell below that standard.

items.question: How long do I have to file a medical malpractice claim after treatment in Fresno County?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discovered or reasonably should have discovered the injury, but no more than three years from the date it occurred. There are limited exceptions, so it's worth getting a records review sooner rather than later.

items.question: What is the 90-day notice I've heard about?
items.answer: California requires that you notify the healthcare provider at least 90 days before filing a malpractice lawsuit. This step applies whether your care happened at a small Coalinga clinic or a larger regional hospital, and we can help prepare it correctly.
